H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
27-year-old male presents via video consult minutes after a suspected wasp/bee sting to right arm with localized erythematous rash and subjective mild dyspnoea/lip tingling; examination shows no objective airway compromise, consistent with an uncomplicated localized allergic reaction; advised oral antihistamine and emergency precautions.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Struggling to breathe” and concern for swelling after single insect sting.  
• Onset: Sting occurred “a few minutes ago” prior to call.  
• Duration/progression: Symptoms present for several minutes; no objective worsening during consult.  
• Location: Sting on right arm; mild redness/“blotchy” rash with puncture site.  
• Associated symptoms: Subjective slight lip swelling/tingling, “weird” tongue sensation; no visible swelling, no stridor, no generalized urticaria, no syncope, no GI symptoms.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None attempted before consult; reassurance reduced anxiety.  
• Review of systems (pertinent):  
  – Respiratory: Subjective mild dyspnoea; able to speak full sentences.  
  – ENT: No throat tightness, no visible intra-oral swelling.  
  – Skin: Local erythema only; no spreading warmth.  
  – Cardiovascular, GI, GU, Neuro, MSK: Not specifically asked/denied.  
• Past episodes: No prior anaphylaxis; never prescribed EpiPen.

Past Medical History:
• Eczema (previous; details not discussed).  
• Occasional anxiety/panic episodes (never medicated).  
Medications: None routinely; has not yet taken antihistamines.  
Allergies: Penicillin (reaction not specified).

Social History:
• Occupation: Computer scientist.  
• Living situation: Lives alone.  
• Pets: One cat.  
• Tobacco, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.  

Family History:
• No known family illnesses or history of acute allergic reactions reported.

Physical Examination: (video-based)
• General: Conversing comfortably; no distress.  
• Airway/Breathing: Normal speech; no audible stridor; breathing appears normal.  
• Lips/oral cavity: No visible swelling; oropharynx normal.  
• Skin: Right arm—localized erythema/blotchy rash with puncture mark, no significant swelling or heat.  
• Cardiovascular/Abdominal/Neuro: Not assessed.  
• Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
• None performed or required at this stage.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Localized allergic reaction to insect sting  
  Assessment: High likelihood based on isolated cutaneous findings without systemic involvement.  
  Plan:  
  • Start oral antihistamine – e.g., chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, dose/route/frequency per OTC instructions (doctor suggested up to 6×/day) OR a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine.  
  • Observe sting site; if redness spreads, becomes hot, or signs of infection develop, seek medical review (possible antibiotics).  
  • Provide written information link on sting reactions and anaphylaxis.  

Issue 2 – Risk of early anaphylaxis (currently absent)  
  Assessment: Moderate concern given timing and subjective lip/tongue sensations; no objective findings.  
  Plan:  
  • Educate on red-flag symptoms: lip/tongue/facial swelling, stridor, progressive dyspnoea, widespread urticaria, dizziness/syncope.  
  • Immediate action if symptoms occur: call emergency services or present to nearest Emergency Department.  
  • Low threshold to re-contact primary care for any deterioration.  

Issue 3 – Anxiety secondary to event  
  Assessment: Contributory to sensation of breathlessness.  
  Plan:  
  • Reassurance provided during consult.  
  • Advise patient to seek further support if anxiety persists or worsens.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting – High likelihood; confined erythema and absence of systemic signs.  
2. Early IgE-mediated anaphylaxis – Moderate likelihood; compatible timing but no objective airway/skin involvement presently.  
3. Anxiety/panic attack – Moderate likelihood; subjective dyspnoea disproportionate to findings; known history of anxiety.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vitals, complete review of systems, full medication reconciliation, detailed allergy reaction, smoking/alcohol history, immunization status.  
• Conflicts: None between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; complete for main complaint but limited ROS and vitals.
